newsitem.title: USA: Toys R Us acquires Baby Superstore.
newsitem.headline: Toys R Us acquires Baby Superstore.

text.p: Toys R Us Inc., the world's largest retailer of children's products, will acquire Baby Superstore Inc. in a stock merger valued at about $376 million, the companies said Wednesday.

Overnight, the toy retailer's three-outlet Babies R Us franchise will become the nation's leading operator of infant and toddler superstores, with 73 stores in 23 states generating sales in excess of $450 million in 1996.

The deal is "another important step in our long range strategic business plan to become the leading retailer in the infant-through-toddler marketplace," said Toys R Us Chief Executive Michael Goldstein.

"Through the excellent strategic fit of this acquisition, we will be able to accelerate our planned growth in sales and profitability of Babies R Us, our new format that is already exhibiting exciting growth potential."
Goldstein also said he expected the acquisition to boost sales and earnings immediately, through lower costs and economies of scale.
Under the definitive agreement, Toys R Us will offer 0.8121 of a share of its stock for each Baby Superstore share in a tax-free exchange, valued at $23.45 as of the close of business on Oct. 1.
Duncan, S.C.-based Baby Superstore's stock jumped $4.25 to $24.125 early on Nasdaq. Toys "R" Us rose $1.375 to $30.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Jack Tate, founder, chairman and chief executive of Baby Superstore, agreed to accept a smaller payment of 0.5150 of a share for each of his Baby Superstore shares, valued at $14.87 as of close of business on Oct. 1.

Tate, Baby Superstore's single largest shareholder with a stake of about 46.8 percent, agreed to vote his shares in favour of the merger. The company has approximately 19.2 million shares outstanding, according to Standard & Poor's.

"Not only will this help to facilitate a transaction of which I have been a strong proponent, but it will also enhance the returns for the remaining shareholders, as well as for those associate option-holders who have helped grow Baby Superstore over the years," Tate said.
The merger, which has been approved by both companies' boards of directors, is expected to close around the end of January, subject to approval by Baby Superstore shareholders.
Baby Superstore operates 70 stores that sell baby and young children's products in 21 states.
Paramus, N.J.-based Toys R Us operates 651 toy stores in the United States, 366 foreign toy stores, including franchise stores, and 211 Kids R Us children's clothing stores.
